alerts.title: Abdominal pain: screen as suspected ADR
alerts.message: Guidelines require all healthcare workers to screen for suspected adverse drug reactions at each encounter using the Drug Safety Screening checklist, and all suspected ADRs should be recorded and reported. Patient presents with abdominal pain today. TDF can cause gastrointestinal toxicity and renal-related abdominal complaints. DTG is also associated with gastrointestinal side effects. Evidence against drug attribution: appetite is preserved and no fever is present, making a drug cause less clear. However, non-drug causes such as infection or other GI pathology should also be evaluated. The clinician's plan does not document ADR screening or any investigation for the abdominal pain.

evidence.recommended_action: Screen abdominal pain as a suspected ADR using the drug safety checklist. Evaluate for non-drug causes. Document findings and report if drug-attributed.

alerts.title: No action plan for abdominal pain
alerts.message: Patient reports abdominal pain but the clinician's assessment and plan only note that appetite is okay, with no diagnostic or therapeutic action documented. Guidelines require that suspected ADRs be recorded into HMIS tools and reviewed. The plan lacks any investigation, symptom management, follow-up instructions, or ADR reporting. Abdominal pain on a TDF-containing regimen warrants evaluation for renal and hepatic causes, as TDF is nephrotoxic and can cause abdominal complaints. No new labs were ordered today.

evidence.recommended_action: Document a diagnostic and management plan for abdominal pain. Consider renal function and liver enzyme testing. Schedule follow-up to monitor symptom resolution.
